deviations.justification: The which-br / `br list --status=open` install-verification probe is deleted; tracker availability is now checked by `toolchain-cli preflight --require`, an availability probe resolved separately and not an execution step. The remaining `br list` calls are the tracker.list reads.

Reads of repository state (current branch, default branch, repo toplevel, remote URL, branch existence) are reworded to state their intent without a literal git command because no workflow.* capability exposes them; for the backend/remote the TRD-039 resolver detection (`toolchain-cli explain`/`resolve`) is the source.

Reads of repository state (current branch, default branch, repo toplevel, remote URL, branch existence) are reworded to state their intent without a literal git command because no workflow.* capability exposes them; for the backend/remote the TRD-039 resolver detection (`toolchain-cli explain`/`resolve`) is the source.

Plain git operations are workflow.* capabilities of the default `plain-git` workflow adapter (branch creation is `git switch -c` via workflow.branch-create, `git switch` already in the sequence); `git checkout -b` and `git town ...` are the non-default git-town path, not part of the unconfigured sequence.

No workflow.* capability stages files (plain-git workflow.commit is `git commit -m` only), so the source now states the staging intent ("stage exactly that path") without a literal `git add`; the agent still stages the same explicit paths before workflow.commit.

`az repos pr create` was the Azure DevOps branch of the PR-creation backend switch; the default host adapter is `github` (toolchain.default.yaml), so the unconfigured sequence opens the change request with `gh pr create` only; the ADO step now lives in the azure-devops adapter behind host.change-request-create.
The pre-refactor closing step was `br update --status=closed` (deduplicated under `br update`); TRD-029 replaces it with tracker.close, whose default template is `br close`.

Pre-refactor `git commit` was only mentioned in the constraints block (prohibiting `commit -a`), i.e. after the workflow steps; the workflow stated the commit in prose. The refactor invokes workflow.commit (`git commit`) at the commit step (after the bead comment, before tracker.sync/close), the position the commit actually occurs in the pre-refactor workflow too.
